text:
alex_k: Quick sync — we need to pick the focus for Q3 perf bets: invest in kernel-level fusions for MQA attention or prioritize dynamic batching + smarter routing. Acme Health is asking for ~50% p95 reduction on 8k-context embeddings path, and Sales says this is a likely Dedicated deal. thoughts?
jess_pm: Can we quantify ETA and risk for both? Sales needs a launch criteria list to justify the commitment.
sarah_l: Kernel fusions are high ROI long-term but 6-8w dev + validation. Dynamic batching + routing is lower dev time but might not hit 50% on p95.
yun_chen: Quick numbers from recent microbenchmarks: optimized MQA kernel gives ~30-40% token throughput boost on A100 80GB for seq len 8k. Dynamic batching reduced median latency but p95 only improves ~15% under bursty traffic.
yun_chen: attaching a quick repro command:```bash
./bench --model redwood-mqa-8k --profile kernels,kv --batcher=dynamic --concurrency=16 --seq=8192
```
mike_r: Also consider KV cache memory usage — fused kernels increase per-shard GPU memory by ~1.2GB. That impacts Dedicated packing. Ops wants numbers.
liz_ops: If memory goes up we may need to reduce slots per GPU which affects unit economics. Ops + Sales need tradeoffs spelled out.
alex_k: Good. Can we frame launch criteria (quantitative) for either path so PM can decide? Suggest: p95 <= target_ms, throughput at N concurrent, memory delta, rollout safety checks.
jess_pm: Proposed launch criteria (first draft):
- p50/p95 <= baseline * 0.6 (i.e., >=40% improvement) on target workloads
- sustained throughput at 100 qps with no more than 10% error rate
- memory overhead <= +1.5GB per GPU for Dedicated configs
- end-to-end quality regression <= 1% (customer eval sets)
- canary passes for 48h with automated rollback on latency regressions
Agree?
sarah_l: Those look reasonable. Suggest we split into MUST vs NICE: MUST = p95 improvement >=30%, errors <5%, canary rollback. NICE = 40% p95, +1% quality tolerance.
yun_chen: Also need benchmark harness for customer traffic shapes. I'll generate 3 profiles: steady, bursty, and long-context tails. perf-bot: scheduled build #182 ran: kernels vs batching A100 results uploaded to /s3/perf/182/report.html :thumbsup:
mike_r: Can someone run the Dedicated packing calc if memory goes +1.2GB? I can simulate but need exact per-model numbers.
jess_pm: I'll ask Sales to freeze the Acme SLAs so we have concrete targets.
alex_k: Action items: yun -> generate traffic profiles + run kernel fusion full sweep (due 5d). sarah -> estimate dev effort + test plan for kernels (3w estimate). mike -> Dedicated packing sim (2d). jess -> confirm SLA with Sales (48h). liz -> estimate ops cost delta if memory increases (3d).
yun_chen: I'll post the perf summaries as a short CSV when done. For reference, current p95 on Acme testset = 780ms for embeddings-8k under baseline.
sarah_l: If baseline 780ms, threshold proposals mean MUST p95 <= 546ms (30% improvement) and NICE <=468ms (40%).
jess_pm: ok that's helpful for Sales.
mike_r: One more note: kernel fusions might complicate hotpatching for private deployments. Need rollout/rollback plan in console.
liz_ops: Ops prefers an opt-in flag per-deployment so we can flip back quickly. Also add alerting on memory pressure + OOM guard rails.
alex_k: Agreed. For prioritization: if yun confirms kernels hit MUST numbers within the sweep, we allocate kernel work as top perf bet. If not, we default to batching + routing improvements.
yun_chen: I'll have initial numbers by EOD Friday.
jess_pm: Thanks all — I'll draft an OKR ticket with the launch criteria and link to perf reports.
perf-bot: reminder: weekly perf sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10:00 — agenda will include this thread. :bell:
